questions.question: Which element of security means "keeping information visible only to people who are allowed to see it"?
choices: Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
Reliability
questions.explanation: Confidentiality means that only authorized people can access the information. Integrity means it has not been tampered with, and availability means it can be used when needed.

questions.question: A server failed and a web service became unusable. Which element of CIA was lost?
choices: Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
None of them
questions.explanation: When something cannot be used when it is needed, "availability" has been lost.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to manage passwords?
choices: Use the same password on every service so it is easy to remember
Use your birthday
Use a different long password for each service and manage them with a password manager
Save them in plain text in a notes app and keep it on screen
questions.explanation: If you reuse a password, a leak from one service lets attackers log in to the others. Using a different long password for each service, managed with a password manager, is effective.

questions.question: Which combination counts as multi-factor authentication?
choices: A password and a security question
A password and a verification code sent to your smartphone
Entering the password twice
An ID and a password
questions.explanation: It combines different kinds of factors: a password (knowledge) and a smartphone (possession). A password and a security question are both "knowledge", so they are not multi-factor.

questions.question: Which malware encrypts files so they cannot be used and demands money to restore them?
choices: Worm
Spyware
Ransomware
Adware
questions.explanation: Ransomware is malware that encrypts files and demands a ransom.

questions.question: Which malware does not attach itself to other files, and spreads copies of itself over a network on its own?
choices: Virus
Worm
Trojan horse
Spyware
questions.explanation: A worm runs on its own and multiplies over the network. A virus differs in that it attaches itself to other files.

questions.question: You receive an SMS saying "Your account will be suspended. Please confirm at the following URL within 24 hours." What is the appropriate response?
choices: Open the URL right away and log in
Reply to the SMS to check whether it is genuine
Do not open the URL. Go to the service yourself from the official app or a bookmark and check
Forward it to family and friends as a warning (with the URL as it is)
questions.explanation: Wording that rushes you is typical of phishing (smishing). Do not use the link in the message. Check from the official app or a bookmark.

questions.question: What is phishing by SMS (text message) called?
choices: Smishing
Vishing
Pharming
Skimming
questions.explanation: SMS + phishing gives the name smishing. Vishing uses voice calls.

questions.question: What do you call an attack that targets a software vulnerability after it has been discovered but before a fix has been released?
choices: Brute-force attack
Zero-day attack
DoS attack
Dictionary attack
questions.explanation: If the day the fix is provided is counted as day one, the attack takes place before that (on day zero), so it is called a zero-day attack.

questions.question: What is the main danger of continuing to use an OS whose support has ended?
choices: The screen becomes dark
Newly found vulnerabilities are not fixed
It can no longer connect to the internet
Files are deleted automatically
questions.explanation: Once support ends, updates are no longer provided, so new vulnerabilities are left open and the system becomes easier to attack.

questions.question: Which is the correct description of the "3-2-1 rule" for backups?
choices: Save 2 files on 1 PC once every 3 days
Keep 3 copies of the data, store them on 2 kinds of media, and keep 1 in another place
Have 3 people check, save twice, and keep for 1 year
Save 3 generations to 1 cloud every 2 hours
questions.explanation: The 3-2-1 rule is 3 copies, 2 kinds of media, and 1 in another place (offline or in the cloud).

questions.question: Which way of backing up is especially effective against ransomware?
choices: Save only to an external HDD that is always connected to the PC
Copy to another folder on the same PC
After backing up, keep the backup disconnected from the network and the PC
Take no backups and rely on security software alone
questions.explanation: An always-connected backup may be encrypted by ransomware along with the original. A disconnected (offline) backup is effective.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about a site whose URL begins with "https://"?
choices: It is always a genuine, safe site
The communication is encrypted
It never contains viruses
It is always safe to enter personal information
questions.explanation: HTTPS indicates that the communication is encrypted, but it does not guarantee that the site is genuine. Fake sites can use HTTPS too.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate way to use a cafe's public Wi-Fi that has no password?
choices: Make a bank transfer by online banking
Use a VPN, or avoid important operations
Share a folder with everyone
Turn off security software temporarily
questions.explanation: On unencrypted public Wi-Fi, others may be able to eavesdrop on your traffic. Use a VPN or avoid important operations.

questions.question: When you post a photo on social media, which of these is likely to reveal where you live?
choices: The size of the photo
The photo's location data and the scenery in the background
The file name of the photo
The day of the week you posted
questions.explanation: A place can be identified from the location data embedded in a photo (Exif) or from buildings and scenery in the background.

questions.question: What do you call the situation where information published on the internet can never be fully deleted because it is copied and spread?
choices: Digital tattoo
Digital detox
Digital signage
Digital twin
questions.explanation: It is called a "digital tattoo" because, like a tattoo, it cannot be removed.

questions.question: Product prices on a website were changed by someone without permission. Which element of CIA was lost?
choices: Availability
Integrity
Confidentiality
Anonymity
questions.explanation: The information is no longer correct (it was tampered with), so integrity has been lost.

questions.question: Someone dropped a USB memory stick containing customer information, and a third party who picked it up saw the contents. Which element of CIA was lost?
choices: Confidentiality
Reliability
Availability
Integrity
questions.explanation: The information was seen by someone who was not authorized, so confidentiality has been lost.

questions.question: Which measure is the most appropriate for improving availability?
choices: Putting a password on a file
Adding a digital signature to data
Running two servers so that if one stops, the other keeps working
Encrypting communication
questions.explanation: Availability means "being usable when needed". Passwords and encryption mainly protect confidentiality, and digital signatures mainly protect integrity.

questions.question: What do you call an attack that uses a list of IDs and passwords leaked from one company to try logging in to other services one after another?
choices: Credential stuffing attack
DoS attack
Watering hole attack
Zero-day attack
questions.explanation: This attack takes advantage of reused passwords. Using a different password for each service is the defense.

questions.question: Which of the following passwords is the hardest to guess?
choices: password123
19950812 (your own birthday)
Tanaka2025 (family name + year)
ringo-sora-tokei-kame-27 (a long phrase of unrelated words)
questions.explanation: Length matters most for a password. Common words and personal information such as birthdays and names are easy to guess.

questions.question: Which of these is a "possession" factor in multi-factor authentication?
choices: A fingerprint
The answer to a security question
A password
An authenticator app on a smartphone
questions.explanation: Passwords and security questions are "knowledge", a fingerprint is "biometrics", and a smartphone or security key is "possession".

questions.question: Which malware gets itself installed by pretending to be useful software and then acts maliciously behind the scenes?
choices: Trojan horse
Freeware
Worm
Ransomware
questions.explanation: It is named after the wooden horse in Greek mythology. It gets in by pretending to be useful software. Freeware simply means free software and is not malware.

questions.question: Which malware collects information such as what you type and your browsing history and sends it out without you noticing?
choices: Freeware
Worm
Ransomware
Spyware
questions.explanation: Spyware secretly watches and sends out information. A keylogger, which records keystrokes, is one kind.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an appropriate way to prevent malware infection?
choices: Keeping antivirus software enabled
Keeping the OS and software up to date
Not opening attachments in suspicious emails
Eagerly trying free software of unknown origin
questions.explanation: Software of unknown origin may have malware planted in it. Get software from official sites and official stores.

questions.question: Which is a common feature of phishing emails?
choices: They contain no links at all
They use wording that stirs up anxiety and haste, such as "urgent" or "account suspended"
Your full name is written correctly
They tell you to check from the official app
questions.explanation: Phishing rushes you so that you cannot judge calmly. Note that even an email with your correct name may be a fake that uses leaked information.

questions.question: You entered your ID and password on a phishing site. What is the most appropriate thing to do first?
choices: Change the password right away from the official site, and also change it on other services where you use the same password
Wait and see for a while
Reply to the email and ask them to delete the information
Visit the fake site again and cancel what you entered
questions.explanation: Change the password immediately to prevent damage. If you entered card details, contact the card company too.

questions.question: You receive an email claiming to be from your bank. What is the most reliable way to make sure you reach the real site?
choices: Check that the sender's display name is the bank's name
Do not use the link in the email. Go there yourself from a bookmark or the official app
Check that the linked page shows a padlock (HTTPS)
Check that the email's design looks just like the real one
questions.explanation: Fake sites can use HTTPS, and designs and display names can be copied. Going in yourself through an entrance you trust is the reliable way.

questions.question: What do you call a program distributed to fix a vulnerability in software?
choices: Malware
Patch (fix)
Firewall
Plugin
questions.explanation: Applying a patch (security update) closes the vulnerability that was found.

questions.question: Which is the right way to think about OS and app updates?
choices: Never update, because changes in behavior are a nuisance
Updating everything once a year is enough
Apply updates as soon as possible after they are released (turn on automatic updates)
Updates are unnecessary if you have antivirus software
questions.explanation: Attackers go after disclosed vulnerabilities right away. Turn on automatic updates and apply them early.

questions.question: Which is the correct description of a "vulnerability"?
choices: A security weakness or flaw in software or a system
Software that manages passwords
A kind of computer virus
A mechanism that encrypts communication
questions.explanation: A vulnerability is also called a security hole. If attackers exploit it, it leads to unauthorized access or malware infection.

questions.question: Which statement about backups is correct?
choices: Once you have taken one, you never need to update it
Take them regularly, and check that you can actually restore from them
There is no need to check whether a backup can be restored
Saving to the same drive as the original data is enough
questions.explanation: A backup is useless if you cannot restore from it when it counts. Taking backups regularly and testing restores are both important.

questions.question: What is the problem with using only a cloud sync feature (which automatically keeps a folder on your PC and the cloud identical) in place of a backup?
choices: Sync always has to be done by hand
Syncing stops your communication being encrypted
Photos cannot be stored in the cloud
If a file is deleted or encrypted, that state may be reflected in the synced copy too
questions.explanation: Sync is a feature that "makes things the same", so accidental deletion and encryption by ransomware are reflected too. Use a feature that can go back to earlier versions, or keep a separate backup.

questions.question: What should you do in advance in case your smartphone breaks or is lost?
choices: Back up your photos and contacts regularly
Turn off the screen lock
Stop OS updates
Write your password on paper and stick it on the device
questions.explanation: The photos and contacts on a phone can all be lost at once if it breaks or is lost. Back them up regularly to the cloud or a PC.

questions.question: On public Wi-Fi, what is the danger of connecting to a fake access point that has the same name (SSID) as the genuine one?
choices: The Wi-Fi becomes faster
Your traffic may be eavesdropped on, or you may be led to fake sites
Installed apps are deleted automatically
The phone's battery just runs down faster
questions.explanation: A fake access point (an "evil twin") relays your traffic while eavesdropping on it or altering it.

questions.question: Which is the best description of a VPN?
choices: A mechanism that creates an encrypted, virtual private channel over the internet
A mechanism that makes websites load faster
A feature that generates passwords automatically
Software that removes viruses
questions.explanation: With a VPN, third parties are less able to see your traffic, even on public Wi-Fi.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about a website that shows a padlock (HTTPS)?
choices: A padlock means you can be certain the site is safe
Sites with a padlock do not store personal information
The communication is encrypted, but the site itself is not necessarily genuine or safe
You cannot be infected with a virus by viewing a site with a padlock
questions.explanation: These days many phishing sites use HTTPS too. The padlock only shows that "the communication is encrypted".

questions.question: Which information, if written on social media, is likely to be a hint for guessing your password or the answer to a "security question"?
choices: Your favorite movie genre
Your pet's name, your birthday, or the school you went to
A comment on today's weather
A general comment on the news
questions.explanation: Security questions often ask for things like "your pet's name" or "the school you attended". Be careful about making such information public.

questions.question: What is the considerate thing to do when posting a photo taken with a friend on social media?
choices: Add your friend's name and school
Set the audience to "public"
Post it without letting your friend know
Ask the friend in the photo whether it is all right to post it
questions.explanation: Publishing a photo of someone else without permission can invade their privacy and cause trouble.

questions.question: Someone you met on social media says "I want to meet you" or "send me a photo". What is the appropriate response?
choices: Believe their profile and go to meet them alone
Send a photo of your face as asked
Trust them and tell them your home address
Do not send personal information or photos, and if you are worried, talk to your family or someone you trust
questions.explanation: A social media profile is easy to fake. Photos you send can be misused or used to threaten you.

questions.question: Which is the safest way to get a smartphone app?
choices: Get it from the official app store
Install a file sent by someone you do not know
Download it from a link in an SMS
Install a file that was recommended on a message board
questions.explanation: Official stores review apps, so malicious apps find it relatively hard to get in. Even so, check the ratings and the publisher.

questions.question: A flashlight app asks for permission to access your contacts and SMS. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Restart the phone and then allow it
Do not allow it because the feature does not need it, and reconsider using the app at all
Turn up the screen brightness and then allow it
Allow everything because it seems convenient
questions.explanation: An app that asks for permissions unrelated to what it does may be a malicious app that steals information.

questions.question: Which feature should you turn on in case your smartphone is lost or stolen?
choices: A louder ringtone
Find my device (remote lock and remote wipe)
Automatic screen brightness
Automatic game saves
questions.explanation: With find-my-device turned on, you can check the location, lock the phone remotely and erase its data if it is lost.

questions.question: What must you do before selling or giving away a smartphone you no longer need?
choices: Delete only the photos
Replace the screen protector
Sign out of your accounts and reset the device to erase the data
Charge it to 100%
questions.explanation: If you do not reset it, the next owner may be able to see your photos, contacts and login information.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate screen lock setting for a smartphone?
choices: Set no screen lock because it is a nuisance
Write the PIN on a sticky note and keep it in the phone case
Set a PIN that is hard to guess, or biometrics such as fingerprint or face
Use an easy PIN such as "1111" or "1234"
questions.explanation: A simple PIN is guessed quickly. The screen lock is the first barrier protecting your information if the phone is lost.

questions.question: While browsing a website, an alarm sounds and the screen says "Your device is infected with a virus. Call this number now." What is the appropriate response?
choices: Call the number shown right away
Do not call. Close the browser (if it will not close, end it from Task Manager or restart)
Pay the fee in the way shown on the screen
Install remote-control software as instructed
questions.explanation: This is a fake warning from a tech support scam. The screen is just a web page, and in most cases closing the browser solves it.

questions.question: Someone claiming to be from a support desk says "Buy electronic money (a gift card) at a convenience store for the repair fee and tell me the number." Which is correct?
choices: It is safe if you tell them only half of the number
It is a typical scam, so you must not tell them the number
It is a payment method often used by genuine support
It is fine if the amount is small
questions.explanation: Electronic money can be spent as soon as the number is passed on, and it is hard to get back. A genuine company never asks for payment this way.

questions.question: Which is a common feature of fake shopping sites?
choices: You can choose from several payment methods
Extremely discounted prices, with bank transfer to an account in an individual's name as the only payment method
The operator's address and phone number are stated and can be confirmed as real
Products are sold at around the usual market price
questions.explanation: Products that are far too cheap, unnatural wording, and a payee account in an individual's name are danger signs.

questions.question: A fake tech support warning is shown in full screen and you cannot find the close button. Which operation is usually suggested for leaving full screen?
choices: Hold down the Esc key
Move the mouse quickly
Call the number shown on the screen
Press the Enter key repeatedly
questions.explanation: Holding down the Esc key often exits full screen. If that does not work, end the browser from Task Manager or restart the PC.

questions.question: Where is it appropriate to turn for advice when you are in trouble with online fraud (in Japan)?
choices: The phone number shown on the fake warning screen
A business found on social media that says it can "get your money back"
The Consumer Hotline (188) or IPA's Information Security Safety Consultation Service
The reply address of the scam email
questions.explanation: Use public consultation services. Businesses that say they can "get your money back" are often scams aiming for a second round of damage.

questions.question: What is the system that looks up an IP address from a domain name called?
choices: HTTPS
SNS
VPN
DNS
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) works like the internet's phone book.

questions.question: In the URL "https://www.example.co.jp.login-check.com/account", which domain actually runs the site?
choices: www.example.co.jp
account
example.co.jp
login-check.com
questions.explanation: You judge a domain from its end. Even with "www.example.co.jp" at the front, the real domain is "login-check.com".

questions.question: In the URL "https://www.example.co.jp/news/", what does the "https" part represent?
choices: The location of the page (path)
The user name
How to communicate (scheme)
The domain name
questions.explanation: https indicates the communication method: "communicate using encrypted HTTP".

questions.question: If the genuine domain is "example.com", which of these is most likely a fake domain?
choices: www.example.com
examp1e.com
shop.example.com
support.example.com
questions.explanation: "examp1e.com" is a fake domain in which "l" (the letter L) has been replaced with "1" (the number one). Names with a subdomain in front of example.com are managed by the same organization.

questions.question: Which is the correct description of an IP address?
choices: A number that identifies a device on the internet (like an address)
The password of a website
Another name for an email address
The name of a virus
questions.explanation: In IPv4 it is written as four numbers, such as "203.0.113.10".

questions.question: Which is correct about an attachment named "invoice.pdf.exe"?
choices: It is an image file
It is a PDF file, so it is safe to open
It is actually an executable file (.exe) and may be malware
It has two extensions, so it cannot be opened
questions.explanation: The last extension shows the real type. A double extension made to look like ".pdf" is a typical malware trick.

questions.question: You are sending one announcement email to 10 business partners. Where do you put the addresses so that they cannot see each other's email addresses?
choices: To
CC
Subject
BCC
questions.explanation: Addresses in To and CC are visible to every recipient. Addresses in BCC are not shown to the other recipients.

questions.question: You open an attached Word document and an "Enable Content" button appears. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Click it, check the content, and delete it if there is a problem
Click it right away to see the content
Forward it to someone else and have them open it
If you do not recognize the sender or the content, close it without clicking, and if necessary confirm with the sender by another means
questions.explanation: Enabling it runs macros, which can infect you with malware (a technique used heavily by Emotet, among others).

questions.question: The sender's display name on an email is "XX Bank". Which is correct?
choices: Only a bank can set that display name
If the display name is a bank's name, it is always genuine
If the display name is correct, the attachments are safe too
The display name can be set freely, so it alone does not prove the email is genuine
questions.explanation: Anyone can set any display name. Do not casually open links or attachments in the message.

questions.question: Which Windows setting helps you notice disguised file extensions?
choices: Changing the desktop wallpaper
Raising the screen resolution
Emptying the Recycle Bin
Turning on the setting that shows file name extensions
questions.explanation: If you show "File name extensions" from the View menu in File Explorer, you can see the real type, such as ".exe".

questions.question: Which of these should you avoid entering into a generative AI service?
choices: A request to summarize publicly available news
Customers' names and addresses, or unpublished company information
A question about a cooking recipe
A question about the meaning of an English word
questions.explanation: What you enter may be stored or used to train the AI. Do not enter personal information or secrets.

questions.question: Which is the right way to think about answers from generative AI?
choices: AI answers are always correct, so you can use them as they are
You can judge an answer to be correct if it is long
You can judge an answer to be correct if it sounds confident
They can contain plausible-sounding mistakes, so check important matters against another source
questions.explanation: Generative AI sometimes gives answers that differ from the facts but sound plausible (hallucinations). Check important matters on an official site or the like.

questions.question: You get a call in a voice just like a family member's saying "I caused an accident. Please transfer money right away." What is the right response?
choices: Hang up, then call back on a number you already know to check
Transfer the money right away, because the voice is theirs
Call back on the number the caller gives you
Tell the caller your account PIN
questions.explanation: AI can fake a voice so that it sounds real. Check by calling back on a number you already know, not one the caller gives you.

questions.question: Which is the correct reason why passkeys resist phishing?
choices: Because the password is very long
Because a verification code arrives by SMS every time
They are tied to the domain of the site where they were registered and cannot be used on a fake site
Because the user answers a secret question
questions.explanation: A passkey only works on the domain of the site where it was registered. It cannot be used on a fake site that looks the same, so it cannot be tricked out of you.

questions.question: Which is correct about verification codes sent by SMS?
choices: A verification code can be used over and over again
If you enter one on a fake site, the attacker can use it right away to get in
It is fine to tell someone else your verification code
If you use verification codes, you will never be a victim of phishing
questions.explanation: There is a method in which a code you are tricked into entering on a fake site is used on the real site at once (real-time phishing). Codes, too, must not be entered on fake sites.

questions.question: When you register a passkey, what is stored by the site?
choices: The private key
An image of your fingerprint
The PIN for your device's screen lock
The public key
questions.explanation: Only the public key is stored by the site. The private key stays on the device, and information such as your fingerprint is not sent to the site either.
